text:
acme_ops: Hey team — noticed our invoice for Feb has ~3x the tokens compared to the dashboard (dashboard shows ~120k, invoice shows ~360k). We're confident our traffic didn't spike. Any ideas?

maria-support: Thanks for flagging — sorry about the surprise. Can you paste a couple of request IDs and the endpoint you used? Also which model/route?

acme_ops: Sure. Example requests: req_43f21, req_43f22, req_43f23. Endpoint: POST /v1/generate (model: redwood-open-7b). Most requests are short chats (~80-120 tokens).

kevin-billing: I pulled the invoice rows for your account id acct_0042. The billed token metric comes from the metering pipeline that consumes events from the serving runtime. Dashboard shows the "served_tokens" aggregation computed in the UI cache. They should match but not always when there are recent config changes or certain runtime behaviors.

lee-runtime: Quick theory — we recently deployed continuous-batching improvements that coalesce many small chat requests into single large batched calls to the model. Metering currently records tokens before we apply some runtime-level prefix/KV cache deduping logic. In some cases that can inflate billed tokens relative to the UI's served_token number (which is computed after cache accounting).

acme_ops: So invoice > dashboard because metering double-counted tokens that got deduped later? That makes sense. How can we confirm?

maria-support: Can you run one of the request IDs and grab the raw runtime trace? If you have the trace id for req_43f21 we can grep our logs. If not, we can pull traces from our side — need permission to access traces for acct_0042.

acme_ops: I just enabled trace sharing for support (granted via console). Trace for req_43f21 is trace-20240212-7b-01.

lee-runtime: I see the trace. Snippet from runtime trace (abbreviated):

```
# trace-20240212-7b-01
incoming_batch: [req_43f21, req_43f22, req_43f23]
pre_batch_token_count: 3 * ~110 = 330 tokens
kv_cache_hits: prefix cache hit for req_43f22 (saved ~95 tokens)
post_cache_served_tokens_to_model: 165 tokens
metering_event_emitted: tokens_counted_for_billing = pre_batch_token_count (330)
```

lee-runtime: So the bug is that the metering event emitted upstream used the pre-batched token sum instead of the post-cache served token count. That creates a delta when cache hits occur.

kevin-billing: Thanks — that explains the 3x in aggregate for your workload (many short requests got merged and some had prefix cache hits). We'll create a corrective credit for Feb while we fix the pipeline.

maria-support: Next steps: 1) we will issue a billing credit for the discrepant delta (ticket #SUP-1192). 2) engineers will patch metering to use post-cache served_tokens. 3) we can offer to toggle continuous batching off for you while we validate the fix if you'd like.

acme_ops: Appreciate that. Can we toggle batching off immediately? We want predictable billing while you patch.

lee-runtime: Yes — we can flip continuous batching per-account. To disable from our side:

```
PATCH /v1/accounts/acct_0042/config
{ "continuous_batching": false }
```

I'll queue the change now and follow up once it's rolled.

sre-bot: deploy:patch-metrics-fix started by lee-runtime (deploy id dpl-7781). ETA ~2h for canary, 6h full rollout.

kevin-billing: I've started the credit workflow. Expect a provisional credit on next invoice; final adjustment after validation.

acme_ops: Thanks all — we'll leave batching off for now and watch next bill. Please keep us posted on the metrics fix. :thumbsup:

maria-support: Following up in #support once the fix is live and the credit posts. If you notice any other invoice/dash mismatches, ping me directly.

lee-runtime: quick note for internal docs: metering must read tokens after cache/batching logic (post-serve accounting). Filed internal PR with tests (runtime pr #4228).

kevin-billing: Logged SUP-1192 and billing adjustment. Closing the loop once dpl-7781 completes.

acme_ops: A few days later — confirm credit applied, numbers look aligned. Thanks everyone! :tada:
